title: OLTP vs OLAP: Know the Difference

scenes.say: Ever wonder why some databases fly through transactions, while others crunch huge reports? Let's break down OLTP and OLAP.

scenes.label: OLTP
scenes.sub: Handles lots of quick, atomic transactions. Prioritizes speed and data integrity.
scenes.say: OLTP stands for online transaction processing. Think banking apps, where every update has to be fast and reliable.

scenes.label: OLAP
scenes.sub: Optimized for complex queries and aggregations on big data.
scenes.say: OLAP is online analytical processing. It's built for deep dives—like sales reports across regions and years.
OLTP is all about speed and consistency for transactions. OLAP is tuned for heavy analytics, often using denormalized tables for faster queries.

scenes.question: Should you always normalize your schema?
scenes.right: Nope. Normalize for OLTP, but denormalize for OLAP to speed up analytics.
scenes.say: Here's a common trap: always normalizing your schema. That's great for OLTP, but OLAP needs denormalized data for quick analytics.
